chunks.title: Drain Cleaning FAQs
chunks.content: Q: What drain cleaning services do you offer? A: We provide residential and commercial drain cleaning for bathroom sinks, showers, bathtubs, laundry drains, kitchen sink drains, storm drains, toilet drains, floor drains, and main sewer lines. xPlumber can unclog and clean all types of plumbing drains. Q: How long does drain cleaning take? A: Simple jobs, like sink or bathtub drain cleaning, typically take less than an hour. Larger branch line or main sewer jobs and complex pipe blockages can take several hours to a full day. Q: How much does xPlumber charge for drain cleaning? A: Pricing varies based on factors such as the type of drain, the type of clog, the job size, and the necessary services and equipment required, including mechanical snaking, hydrojetting equipment, and video pipe inspection camera snake. Q: Do you offer emergency drain cleaning? A: Absolutely. xPlumber provides emergency drain cleaning services 365 days a year, seven days a week. Q: How do I find drain cleaning near me? A: Check the xPlumber Locations page to find local drain cleaning services.

chunks.title: Emergency Plumbing FAQs
chunks.content: Q: If I have a flood emergency in my home, what can I do to help alleviate the problem? A: Turn off your main water supply immediately to stop flooding if the water is coming from a plumbing pipe, water appliance, or fixture. Move valuables to higher ground and use towels or a wet/dry vacuum to contain water. Call a licensed emergency plumber right away. Q: When to call an emergency plumber? A: Call if you experience plumbing-related flooding, burst pipes, no water supply, sewage backups, or major leaks that risk property damage or health hazards. Q: Can you call 911 for a plumbing emergency? A: No, 911 is reserved for life-threatening emergencies. For plumbing emergencies, contact a licensed emergency plumber or your local utility company. Calling 1-800-GET-ROTO will get you a fast emergency response. Q: What should I do while waiting for xPlumber to arrive during a plumbing emergency? A: Ask the customer service representative if there is anything you need to do before the technician arrives. For instance, if you have a broken water supply pipe, they may tell you to turn off the water to your home until the plumber arrives. Q: What is the response time for a plumbing emergency? A: In most cases, a xPlumber service technician arrives within two hours of your call. If the entire community is dealing with flooding due to a storm or natural disaster, response time will be longer as calls are handled in the order received.

chunks.title: Clear Your Clogged Drain Without Chemicals
chunks.content: Three chemical-free ways to open clogged drains: 1) Plunger - For sinks/tubs use red plungers with shallow cup. Place over drain, push down for vacuum seal, pump up and down 5-6 times, pull backward. 2) Wire clothes hanger - Straighten hanger, bend hook narrow/shallow, remove drain cover, push down until resistance, twist in circle, slowly pull back to capture hair clogs. 3) Baking soda and vinegar - Pour pot of boiling water down drain, follow with 1/2 cup baking soda, wait 5 minutes, pour 1 cup vinegar, let sit 20 minutes. Works best on bathroom sink drains, less effective on kitchen drains. If home remedies don't work, call a professional drain cleaner from xPlumber.

chunks.title: Calcium Buildup in Drains and Pipes
chunks.content: Q: What dissolves calcium buildup in pipes? A: Calcium buildup (limescale) can be dissolved by acids but buildup in copper pipes is rare. If hard water buildup occurs, install a water softener. CLR drain cleaner can reduce buildup on outside of fixtures but is toxic and not recommended for internal pipe treatment. Vinegar can dissolve calcium but would require leaving it in pipes for at least 24 hours and the taste may linger. A better solution is to replace pipes with PEX plastic pipes, which are completely resistant to mineral build-up and provide higher pressures and water flow rates than copper pipe.

chunks.title: Water Damage Restoration FAQs
chunks.content: Q: How quickly can xPlumber respond to water damage? A: xPlumber is available 24/7 for emergency water damage cleanup. Q: Can you vacuum flood water? A: xPlumber uses powerful professional-grade water extraction vacuums to remove water and sewage. Q: What happens to water damaged furniture after a flood? A: Unsalvageable contents including wet and contaminated carpeting, padding, flooring, saturated drywall, insulation, and furniture are removed. What can be salvaged depends on the type of water contamination (clean water, gray water, or black water). Q: What should we do after water damage? A: Contact xPlumber immediately for assessment, water removal, drying, cleaning/sanitizing, and deodorizing. Implement preventive measures: regular inspections, proper drainage, install sump pump and backup, seal cracks, monitor water usage, install water alarms.
